reason: Checked against the page image myself. I downloaded the OCR, the page-number map and the page image (leaf n260) of the 1841 Boston James Munroe Essays (emersonralessays00emerrich). The page is headed ESSAY X. CIRCLES., has no verse motto, and the page map gives it as p. 249 (signature 11*). The sentence reads exactly as the card: Our life is an apprenticeship to the truth, that around every circle another can be drawn; that there is no end in nature, but every end is a beginning; that there is always another dawn risen on mid-noon, and under every deep a lower deep opens. The comma after truth is there, and the next line This fact, as far as it symbolizes is visibly indented as a new paragraph, so the sentence does close the opening paragraph and the corrected locator is right. Attribution right, Emerson in his own voice, not on the misattribution list. shipped.js: not shipped, no near opening, Emerson 0 of 3 shipped, not banned. In scope, publishable, ends in a full stop, prose. Source line 97 characters, leads with the name, no dash; tag Essay is the form.
